do_not_change.summary: Preserve the lock-first PostgreSQL transaction ordering.
do_not_change.evidence: The first ordered statement locks the candidate Signal/Run source before the conditional release; the staged live PostgreSQL interleaving test exercises terminalization during the release window and verifies that release either does not happen or commits with its successor.
do_not_change.impact: Prevents terminalization from leaving a released controller without a successor decision.
do_not_change.recommendation: Keep this read/lock as the first batch statement and retain the targeted live-provider regression.

do_not_change.summary: Preserve the guarded release and successor-claim predicates.
do_not_change.evidence: The staged code retains exact project/controller/template Action qualification, provider-specific fail-closed instant comparison, and the release-marker-plus-no-active-controller condition. The refreshed verification records passing D1, PostgreSQL, CI, full-suite, and build gates.
do_not_change.impact: Maintains deterministic, tenant-scoped release without duplicate active controllers or orphan graph rows.
do_not_change.recommendation: Do not simplify these conditions without equivalent provider-backed timestamp and concurrency coverage.

do_not_change.summary: Preserve the bounded preflight-only role of cycle selection.
do_not_change.evidence: Preflight selects only the possible cycle key; the repository requalifies candidate source, controller, Action, time, and release in its atomic batch. Staged PostgreSQL service-race coverage validates shared successor identity and graph counts.
do_not_change.impact: Keeps stale reads from granting mutation authority while retaining deterministic retries and successor identities.
do_not_change.recommendation: Keep all release authority in the repository batch.
